doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Bass playing, avant-garde and the state of the music
title: Requests and the hip players who would not play them
summary: A $10 tip for "Milenburg Joys" from a regular, and some hip players refusing requests.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: And I'm happy to be able to do things like that. Sometimes you can make or break a band and have somebody in that band that knows some of those tunes that somebody might want. We had a little gig back in the '40s, when I come out of service, a cat named Mike Walker, saxophone was his instrumentation -- saxophone, guitar and bass -- we worked up on this job about six months. Every night, at least twice a week, this guy would come in and as soon as he walked in the door, he wanted to hear Milenbergy Milenburg Joys. I don't care what we were playing, when we'd see him approach that door to come in, we'd go right into Milenbergy Milenburg Joys. That was a $10 tip each time. So to be able to play those kind of tunes.
Then it got to the point where some of the so-called hip cats won't play the requests, you know. They didn't want to admit they didn't know them.
That would alienate some of the audiences. But that's all part of that avantgarde versus swing, be-bop, whatever.
